title: One successor step of nilpotent reduction lissity
statement: Let a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] be given by a precoverage with isomorphisms, composition, base change and pullbacks. Let B be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], J an ideal, K a bounded-above derived object of sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient ring [def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension], and n at least one. Use finite constant-module local descriptions [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]. If all cohomology sheaves of the derived reductions of K modulo J and modulo J^n have these local descriptions over their respective quotient rings, then all cohomology sheaves of its reduction modulo J^(n+1) have these descriptions over B/J^(n+1). Derived categories and cohomology are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. This asserts one filtration step, without an induction over all powers or a nilpotent specialization.

proof.text: For every Noetherian coefficient ring D, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-lisse-triangle] proves that finite locally constant cohomology in the commutative constant-ring convention is closed under the middle term of distinguished triangles. Its proof explicitly compares the two constant-ring constructions before applying the existing Serre theorem.

source.place: Tag 094I, proof, paragraph beginning 'Recall that the locally constant sheaves'

proof.text: Put D=B/J^(n+1) and Q=J^n/J^(n+1). Regard 0 to Q to D to B/J^n to 0 as an exact sequence of D-modules. Constant sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. Choose a flat K-flat representative P of K by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Tensoring this sequence over B with P preserves exactness degreewise by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Forgetting D-module structure is exact and reflects exactness, so this gives a distinguished triangle of derived D-module sheaves. The middle term computes the reduction modulo J^(n+1), and the last term is the restriction of the reduction modulo J^n, by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Balancing identifies the first term with restriction from B/J of (P tensor_B B/J) tensor_(B/J) Q. The quotient-coefficient complex P tensor_B B/J is K-flat, since its tensor with an acyclic quotient-module complex identifies with P tensor_B that complex, which is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The balancing maps send (p tensor b) tensor q to p tensor bq, with inverse p tensor q to (p tensor 1) tensor q; these commute with differentials and restrictions.

source.place: Tag 094I, proof, displayed distinguished triangles and isomorphisms

proof.text: The ring B/J is Noetherian, and Q is finite over B/J: finite generators of J^n project to generators, and J annihilates Q. Good truncation followed by [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] gives a bounded-above flat K-flat representative of K. Thus its reduction modulo J is bounded above. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor] to this reduction and Q to obtain finite locally constant cohomology over B/J for the first triangle term. The quotient maps D to B/J and D to B/J^n are surjective because n is positive. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-lisse-restriction], restricting along these maps preserves finite constant local models. Hence the first term and, by the previous-reduction hypothesis, the last term have finite locally constant cohomology over D. The quotient D is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-lisse-triangle] over D to conclude the successor reduction, without induction over all powers. Working in D-module sheaves throughout removes the need to recover quotient-linear local models from B-module local models.

theorem locallyConstantFiniteTypeModules_reduction_succ
    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] (T : Precoverage C)
    [T.HasIsos] [T.IsStableUnderComposition] [T.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [T.HasPullbacks]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] (J : Ideal B)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (constantCoefficientRing T.toGrothendieck B))]
    [∀ I : Ideal B, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (constantCoefficientRing T.toGrothendieck (B ⧸ I)))]
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (constantCoefficientRing T.toGrothendieck B)))
    (hbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K))
    (hmod : ∀ i : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantFiniteTypeModules T.toGrothendieck (B ⧸ J)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        ((constantCoefficientScalarExtension T.toGrothendieck (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).obj K)))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hprevious : ∀ i : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantFiniteTypeModules T.toGrothendieck (B ⧸ J ^ n)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        ((constantCoefficientScalarExtension T.toGrothendieck
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n))).obj K))) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantFiniteTypeModules T.toGrothendieck (B ⧸ J ^ (n + 1))
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        ((constantCoefficientScalarExtension T.toGrothendieck
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ (n + 1)))).obj K))
